submitted.rationale: At a 2.06 eV photon energy, only the Fe-oxide (hematite-like) part of the system absorbs strongly. Measured photocurrent rose steadily as V dropped and Fe went up: idx 47 (Fe0.41 V0.49) 2e-8 A < idx 99 (Fe0.73 V0.16) 1.3e-7 A < idx 200 (Fe0.70 V0.11 Cr0.19) 3.2e-7 A. Index 200 has the lowest V fraction in the library, and its extra Cr may also help.

rejected.reason: FeVO4-like Fe:V~1:1 region measured 2e-8 A, about 16x lower than idx 200
Fe-rich but higher V (0.16), measured 1.3e-7 A, below idx 200

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): mp-19770 (Fe2O3-type) MEGNet HSE gap ~2.77 eV; real hematite gap ~2.1 eV is the only system component near the 2.06 eV photon energy, so the most Fe-rich compositions are the best bet for sub-gap-limited absorption at 602 nm. Index 99 is among the most Fe-rich (Fe 0.73).

Uninformative-to-weak support: PBE gap of mp-19770 is 1.53 eV (underestimated), confirming Fe-based oxides absorb near 2.06 eV. Exploring the FeVO4-like Fe:V~1:1 region (index 47) to contrast with the Fe-rich result at index 99.

Largely uninformative (GLLB gap 0.89 eV for mp-19770 is inconsistent across fidelities). Decision driven by measured trend: Fe-rich/low-V (idx 99, 1.3e-7 A) >> Fe:V~1:1 (idx 47, 2e-8 A). Index 200 has the lowest V (0.11) with high Fe (0.70), extending the trend.
